notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id.

This is a THIRD, independent synthetic application (Redwood Digital Forensics Solutions, LLC) against the same true_requirements.json as data/SHOP-PR-26-002435 -- built specifically to add another contradictory example of a fresh shape (a chassis-width conflict: 15 inches wide stated in the Chassis Specifications versus a '17-inch-wide chassis footprint' claimed in a separate Technical Capability Narrative paragraph), distinct from application.txt's GPU-model contradiction and application_b.txt's USB-hub port-count contradiction on this tender.

All other specs are given a clean, fully compliant itemized configuration in this variant since the goal of this pass is specifically to add contradictory-class density and format diversity, not to re-exercise every failure shape again -- the original and application_b.txt already cover the non_compliant/insufficient_information shapes for this tender's hardware specs.
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone.

primary_verdict / primary_verdict_source (added by SFT data-prep pass): a single training-target label per topic, additive -- acceptable_verdicts is unchanged and remains the source of truth for verdict-accuracy scoring. primary_verdict is the pipeline's own correct prediction where one exists (source: pipeline_prediction), else acceptable_verdicts[0] (source: acceptable_verdicts_first). null for topics with acceptable_verdicts: null (excluded from SFT training, same as they're excluded from verdict scoring).
